title: Crystal growth, magnetic, and transport properties of the candidate altermagnet Cr$_{1/4}$NbS$_{2}$
authors: Nashra Pistawala, Martin R. Lees, Geetha Balakrishnan, Daniel A. Mayoh
abstract: Altermagnetism is a rapidly emerging paradigm in condensed matter magnetism, yet the number of experimentally confirmed altermagnetic candidates remains remarkably limited. Cr$_{1/4}$NbS$_2$ has long been theoretically proposed as a promising altermagnet, but there are no reports on experimental investigation of single crystals. Here, we report the successful growth of high-quality single crystals of Cr$_{1/4}$NbS$_2$ and present its structural, thermal, magnetic, and transport properties. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction provides detailed crystallographic information and confirms the hexagonal crystal symmetry ($P6_3/mmc$), one of the criteria for altermagnetic behavior. Resistivity and heat capacity measurements unambiguously identify an antiferromagnetic Néel temperature of $T_N \sim 141$ K. Magnetotransport measurements reveal non-trivial features in the magnetoresistance and Hall response, indicative of quantum diffusive transport phenomena. Cr$_{1/4}$NbS$_2$, synthesized here for the first time in single-crystalline form, therefore serves as an experimental platform for probing the rich spectrum of phenomena predicted for altermagnetic materials.
summary: This paper reports the first successful growth of single crystals of $	ext{Cr}_{1/4}	ext{NbS}_2$, a material proposed to be an altermagnet. By measuring its structural, thermal, and transport properties, the authors confirm its magnetic ordering temperature and observe transport signatures consistent with quantum diffusive behavior, establishing it as a key platform for altermagnetism research.
main_problem: To experimentally investigate altermagnetism, a magnetic order challenging the simple ferromagnetic/antiferromagnetic classification, in the candidate material $	ext{Cr}_{1/4}	ext{NbS}_2$.
main_result: The authors successfully grew high-quality single crystals of $	ext{Cr}_{1/4}	ext{NbS}_2$, confirming its hexagonal structure and observing signatures of quantum diffusive transport in magnetotransport measurements.
method: The study employed a combination of techniques, including single-crystal X-ray diffraction, heat capacity measurements, and magnetotransport measurements on single crystals.
model_or_system: The physical system is $	ext{Cr}_{1/4}	ext{NbS}_2$, a transition metal-intercalated transition metal dichalcogenide (TMD) proposed to exhibit altermagnetism. Its structure is confirmed to be hexagonal ($P6_3/mmc$), which is crucial for its magnetic properties.
key_observables: Antiferromagnetic Néel temperature ($T_N \sim 141 	ext{ K}$), non-trivial magnetoresistance and Hall response, and hexagonal crystal symmetry.
important_parameters: Temperatures ranging from 1.8 K to 300 K; magnetic fields up to 9 T.
main_assumptions: The study assumes that the observed magnetic and transport features are indicative of the predicted altermagnetic behavior, and that single-crystal measurements are necessary to probe anisotropic properties.
figures_summary: Figure 1(a) shows the grown single crystals, and Figure 1(b) confirms the six-fold symmetry using Laue back-scattering diffraction.
paper_structure: The paper follows a standard experimental structure: introduction establishing the need to study altermagnets, detailed characterization of the single crystals (structural, thermal, magnetic), and finally, transport measurements to confirm the predicted quantum phenomena.
why_interesting: The investigation of altermagnetism in layered TMDs connects concepts of magnetic ordering, electronic structure, and transport phenomena, which are central themes in strongly correlated electron systems research.
